statement: Median per-capita disposable income growth < mean growth in 2027 annual data (national statistics office; one indicator per leading jurisdiction)
status_at_phase_end: Bloc B statistics office, in-phase releases: 2023 annual median growth below mean (5.3% vs 6.3% nominal), but every 2024 cumulative release showed median growth ABOVE mean - Q1 6.4% vs 6.2%, H1 5.9% vs 5.4%, Jan-Sep 5.9% vs 5.2% (property income +1.2%). So in 2024 the condition was not holding; it flipped back only in 2025 releases. Bloc A has no comparable per-capita disposable median/mean pair. No AI signal either way.

items.summary: Bloc B 2023 annual household survey: mean per-capita disposable income +6.3% (nominal), median +5.3%; median 84.2% of mean. Median growth below mean growth.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS '2023年居民收入和消费支出情况' (2024-01-17, verified): mean 39,218 yuan, median 33,036 yuan; urban median +4.4% vs urban mean +5.1%. 2023 growth partly reflects the low 2022 base.

items.summary: Bloc B Q1 2024: median per-capita disposable income +6.4% vs mean +6.2% (nominal); median 82.0% of mean. Median growth above mean growth.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS Q1 2024 income release (2024-04-16, verified via web_extract (review)): mean 11,539 yuan, median 9,462 yuan; urban median +5.7% vs urban mean +5.3%.

items.summary: Bloc B H1 2024: median per-capita disposable income +5.9% vs mean +5.4% (nominal); median growth above mean growth. Property income +2.1%.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS H1 2024 income release (2024-07-15, verified via web_extract (review)): mean 20,733 yuan, median 17,358 yuan; urban median +4.7% vs urban mean +4.6%.

items.summary: Bloc B Jan-Sep 2024: median per-capita disposable income +5.9% vs mean +5.2% (nominal), gap -0.7 pp; median 84.0% of mean. Property income +1.2% vs wage income +5.7%.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS '2024年前三季度居民收入和消费支出情况' (2024-10-18, verified): mean 30,941 yuan, median 25,978 yuan; urban median +4.4% vs urban mean +4.5%.

items.summary: Bloc A annual income report for 2023: real median household income rose ~4% to ~$80,600, the first significant increase since 2019. Pre-tax household money income, not per-capita disposable, so not directly comparable.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau 'Income in the Bloc A: 2023' (P60-282), released 2024-09-10. Values from memory of release coverage; not verified via web_extract this run.

items.summary: No Bloc A official series publishes per-capita disposable-income median and mean growth side by side; a comparable Bloc A series must be constructed. Same gap as later phases.
items.detail: CPS ASEC = pre-tax household money income; BEA distribution of personal income is a prototype/annual research series.
